gloss: To give up halfway; to abandon a task before completing it.
teaser: Today, we explore the importance of perseverance and not giving up.
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Today, we explore the importance of perseverance and not giving up. [break 1s] The phrase is: 半途而废, bàn tú ér fèi. [break 0.5s] 半 (bàn) - half [break 0.5s] 途 (tú) - way [break 0.5s] 而 (ér) - and [break 0.5s] 废 (fèi) - to give up [break 1s] So, 半途而废 literally means "to give up halfway" and figuratively means to abandon a task before completing it. [break 1s] Here’s the story behind it: [break 1.5s] This idiom originates from ancient Chinese literature, where it was used to describe someone who starts a journey or task with enthusiasm but loses motivation midway. It highlights the frustration of seeing potential wasted and emphasizes the importance of seeing things through to the end. [break 1.5s] Here are three examples: [break 1s] 他做事情总是半途而废。 [break 0.5s] He always gives up halfway in everything he does. [break 1s] 如果你半途而废，就永远无法成功。 [break 0.5s] If you give up halfway, you will never succeed. [break 1s] 学习需要坚持，不能半途而废。 [break 0.5s] Learning requires persistence; you can't give up halfway. [break 1s] So remember, 半途而废 means to give up halfway. Thank you for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom. [break 1s]
